name: Stratos Capital & Trust Optimizer
tag: A sandbox for planning credit use, card rewards and keeping personal and business assets separate.

scenarios.title: Plan card rewards
scenarios.ask: I spend ${spend} a month across {cards} cards. Show where each purchase should go to earn the most.
steps: Grouped ${spend} of sample monthly spend into travel, fuel, software, supplies and other.
Matched each category to the best of your {cards} cards.
Checked category caps and annual fees so the plan isn't overstated.
followups: Should business spend go on personal cards?
The sandbox keeps them apart. Mixing business and personal spending makes bookkeeping harder and can weaken the separation between you and your company.
Yes. The full model subtracts fees, so a card only wins a category if its rewards beat its cost.

scenarios.title: Plan a credit cycle
scenarios.ask: I have ${limits} in total limits and carry ${balance}. Plan statement payments to keep utilization low.
steps: Mapped sample statement and due dates for each account.
Scheduled a payment of ${=max(0, round(balance - limits * target / 100))} before statements close.
Set alerts 3 days before each statement date.
followups: Why pay before the statement closes?
Many issuers report the statement balance. Paying earlier lowers the balance that gets reported.
Does this change what I owe?
No. You pay the same amount, just earlier in the cycle.

scenarios.title: Check asset separation
scenarios.ask: Review {entities} entities and {accounts} accounts for mixing between personal and business assets.
steps: Drew the sample structure of {entities} entities, from the trust down to each operating LLC.
Matched {accounts} accounts to their owners. {=max(0, accounts - entities * 2)} accounts have no clear owner.
Flagged {mixed} transactions where personal and business money crossed without a record.
Wrote steps: written agreements, reimbursements, and one account set per entity.

result.title: Separation review
rows: Review the structure with an attorney and CPA

followups: Keeping each entity's money separate and documented supports the liability protection the structure is meant to give. Mixing can weaken it.
It drafts reimbursement entries and notes for the {mixed} flagged items. Your bookkeeper reviews and records them.
